Note::upper¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::upper() const

Case-Fold Every Cell To Uppercase¶

upper() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with every text cell uppercased. It is the mirror of lower: reach for it when the downstream consumer expects capitals — a code or country field, a display header, a case-insensitive key you happen to normalize upward.

Like lower, the mapping is full Unicode uppercase, not ASCII-only. Accented Latin letters (é → É), Greek (α → Α), and Cyrillic all fold, and locale-independent special cases apply: German ß uppercases to SS, so a cell can grow in length. upper() is therefore shape-preserving but not byte-length-preserving. It changes case only — no trimming, no punctuation removal, no Unicode-form normalization — and is idempotent.

For a caseless comparison key, prefer casefold, which is designed for that and handles a few more edge cases; upper() is for output that should read as capitals.

Example 1: A One-Dimensional Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"  Ada lovelace  ", "grace HOPPER", "café"}).upper())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["  ADA LOVELACE  ", "GRACE HOPPER", "CAFÉ"]

Case changes; the leading and trailing spaces are untouched.

Example 2: A Scalar¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note("HeLLo, world").upper();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"HELLO, WORLD"

Example 3: Shape Is Preserved¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout,
                   pluss::make_note({{"ab", "cD"}, {"Ef", "gh"}}).upper())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["AB", "CD"], 
  ["EF", "GH"]
]

Example 4: Full Unicode, Including ß → SS¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"café", "αβγ", "ß"}).upper())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["CAFÉ", "ΑΒΓ", "SS"]

ß has no single uppercase form, so it expands to SS and that cell grows by one byte.

Example 5: Idempotent¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::make_note({"ALREADY"}).upper().upper())
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["ALREADY"]

See Also¶

  • Note::lower: the lowercase counterpart.

  • Note::casefold: aggressive folding for caseless matching keys.

  • Note::title / Note::capitalize / Note::swapcase: partial-case transforms (ASCII-only).
